citations.title: Chapter 02 Administrative Requirements for Licensees (.01-1 through .14)
citations.requirement: Chapter table of contents fetched. It lists .01 Incorporation by Reference, .01-1 License Required, .02 Application, .03 Investigation, .04 Compliance Monitoring, .05 New Site/Closure/Relocation, .06 Licensed Capacity, .07 IFC, .08 Governing Body, .09 PSP, .10 Policies and Procedures, .11 Staffing, .12 Health and Safety, .13 Records, .14 Quality Assurance. Authority: Health-General §§7-904 and 7-909.

citations.title: License Required
citations.requirement: A license is required to provide community residential services. Taken from the fact-checked research; the text was not re-fetched.

citations.title: Application for Initial License or Renewal
citations.requirement: A.(1): the licensee must be a Maryland corporation, or a foreign corporation registered in MD. A.(2)-(3): the governing body is legally responsible for overseeing all programs and for compliance. A.(4): the application needs a business plan, a DD experience summary, prior licensing reports from the last 10 years, and a DDA-approved QA plan. B.: file renewal at least 60 days before the license expires. D.: the Director may approve, approve with conditions, deny, or request more information. F.: voluntary surrender needs a closure schedule submitted at least 90 days ahead and approved by the Director. G.: terminate services to an individual only for good cause with the Director's written approval. Give the Director 90 days' written notice, give the individual and proponent written notice of the right to a hearing under COMAR 10.22.16, and copy the regional office and team. Services are considered terminated after 60 consecutive days' absence unless the Director decides otherwise.

citations.title: Investigation by the Administration
citations.requirement: Sets OHCQ investigation priorities. Priority 1 (immediate jeopardy) investigations start within 2 working days. Taken from the fact-checked research. NOTE: the fetched text of .04E, not .03, contains the 10-working-day plan-of-correction rule; cite .04E for the POC deadline.

citations.title: Compliance Monitoring
citations.requirement: A.: OHCQ, as the Administration's agent, monitors and inspects licensees. B.: an on-site pre-licensure survey is required. C.: announced and unannounced licensure visits happen at least annually. D.: announced or unannounced complaint investigation visits. E.: submit a plan of correction (POC) at the exit conference or within 10 working days of receiving the findings. OHCQ may require it sooner, and the OHCQ Director may grant an extension of up to 30 days. F.: if a POC is unacceptable, resubmit a revised POC within 10 working days.

citations.title: New Site, Site Closure, or Relocation
citations.requirement: DDA approval is required at least 30 days in advance to open, close or relocate a site. Taken from the fact-checked research.

citations.title: Licensed Capacity
citations.requirement: The license states the number of people that may be served. Exceeding it requires Director approval, for a maximum of 60 days plus one 60-day extension. Taken from the fact-checked research.

citations.title: Governing Body
citations.requirement: Board membership must include at least 1 person with a DD, 1 family member of a person with a DD, and 1 person with DD experience. At least 75% of members must live in MD or within 100 miles. No employees or their immediate family may be voting members. Bylaws must cover oversight, compliance, mission/budget/policy approval, conflict of interest, POC responses and PSP approval. Board members and employees may not own property leased back to the licensee (.08C(9)). Taken from the fact-checked research.

citations.title: Program Service Plan (PSP)
citations.requirement: A.: a PSP is required for each service the licensee provides. B.: submit a revised PSP for DDA approval before implementing changes. C.: the administrative head ensures the governing body reviews and updates the PSP at least every 3 years. D.: comply with the approved PSP. E.: contents are rationale, scope, staffing and training, and setting and location (including the number of individuals expected to be served).

citations.title: Policies and Procedures
citations.requirement: A.(1)-(19) requires written policies on: health and safety per the IP; fundamental rights (Health-General §7-1002); promoting choice; confidentiality (Health-General §7-1010); a grievance process with anti-retaliation safeguards; nondiscrimination; reporting and investigating all incidents under DDA procedures; medication administration per DDA's curriculum; compliance with COMAR 10.27.11; behavior safeguards; property-damage payment; Health-General §5-605; no conflict of interest; GAAP fiscal practices; protection of individuals' finances (A(15)(a)-(e)); infection control and standard precautions; a disaster and evacuation plan with sufficient drills; and no individual performing paid staff duties or non-household tasks (A(18)-(19)). B.: group homes need an emergency plan covering evacuation or 72-hour shelter-in-place, an annual practice drill coordinated with local emergency planners, an after-action report and improvement plan, ID with health information, family and DDA regional office notification, staff recall, continuity of operations, off-site data backup, sharing the plan with local emergency management, and an executive summary for families on request. C.: all staff, care providers, consultants and volunteers must know and implement every policy. D.: give each individual and proponent enough information about the grievance process to use it.

citations.title: Staffing Requirements
citations.requirement: A.: analyze the number of individuals and each person's needs, then develop and implement a staffing plan that meets health and safety needs and delivers the IP services. There is no fixed numeric ratio. B.: no employing or contracting with anyone whose criminal history indicates behavior potentially harmful to individuals (Health-General §19-1902 et seq.; COMAR 12.15.03). C.: before independent duties, staff need job training, DDA-approved training (seizure disorders, principles of behavior change, management of disruptive behaviors, medication administration, aging) and OSHA blood-borne pathogens training under 29 CFR 1910.1030. D.: within 3 months of hire, DDA-approved training on community integration, individual-directed planning, characteristics and needs, First Aid/CPR (American Red Cross or equivalent), fundamental rights, communicable diseases, supporting choice, and communication skills. E.: written job descriptions and a policy to prevent employment discrimination.

citations.title: Health and Safety Requirements
citations.requirement: A.: each home must meet local zoning (except as provided in Health-General §7-603), local and State building codes and life-safety requirements, be free of hazards, and be in good repair. B.: free of fire hazards, with adequate smoke detectors, working and updated fire extinguishers, and a written fire evacuation plan. C.: water temperature at a maximum of 110°F unless every resident can regulate it safely and this is documented in each IP. D.: administer medication per DDA's medication curriculum, use unit-dose packaging for oral solids unless the IP says otherwise, package medication for absent individuals separately, and request pharmacy-generated MARs, TARs and physician order forms.

citations.title: Records
citations.requirement: A.: keep each individual's records at the site where the person is served. B.: minimum contents are application identifying information, emergency contact, next of kin, physician, diagnosis, allergies, medication list, the IP (COMAR 10.22.05), documentation of IP implementation, and anything else DDA requires. C.: on a medical emergency, make the person's medical information readily accessible to emergency personnel. D.: keep records at least 6 years, even if the person leaves or dies. Keep current-service documents for as long as the person is served, and organize records for easy access. E.: electronic records must meet the chapter, comply with HIPAA privacy and security rules, and be backed up and stored off-site.

citations.title: Quality Assurance
citations.requirement: A.: submit the QA plan and any substantive changes to DDA for approval. B.: an internal QA system that is focused on individual choice, preference and satisfaction (with personal contact), has measurable outcomes, analyzes trends, responds promptly when health or safety is at risk, and tracks behavior-plan restrictive techniques (who, which technique, date/time, emergency vs. plan, effectiveness). C.: set goals and standards, keep records, and implement changes based on the data. E.: standing committee(s) must review the incident protocol and all incidents, approve all behavior plans that use restrictive techniques, review and set time frames for rights restrictions not related to challenging behavior, and review policies for protection of rights. The committee must have equal numbers of licensee staff and non-employees (individuals, proponents or community members). Members may not decide on incidents or behavior plans they were involved in. It meets as needed with a majority present and must ensure confidentiality under Health-General §7-1010.

citations.title: Scope (Community Residential Services)
citations.requirement: Defines the scope of community residential services (alternative living units, group homes, IFC, CSLA; respite limits). Taken from the fact-checked research; the text was not re-fetched.

citations.title: Staffing and Training (Community Residential Services)
citations.requirement: A.: provide staffing levels and patterns as determined in the IP. B.: provide or arrange training in accordance with COMAR 10.22.02.11.

citations.title: Fundamental Rights

Rule text was not read. .14E(1)(d)-(e) cross-references .03A for restrictions of rights and for behavior plans that use restrictive techniques. Read .03 before finalizing the rights policy text.

citations.requirement: Section number and title confirmed from the Chapter 10 table of contents. Rule text was not read. .14E(1)(d) requires standing-committee approval of behavior plans that use restrictive techniques under 10.22.10.

citations.title: Use of Medications to Modify Challenging Behavior
citations.requirement: Section number and title confirmed from the Chapter 10 table of contents. Rule text was not read.

citations.title: Monitoring Use of Medications to Modify Behavior and Restrictive Techniques
citations.requirement: Section number and title confirmed from the Chapter 10 table of contents and the .14 cross-reference. Rule text was not read.

citations.title: Informal Hearings Under the Maryland Developmental Disabilities Law
citations.requirement: Chapter title confirmed from the link in .02G. Individuals have a right to a hearing under this chapter when services are to be terminated (.02G(2)). Chapter text was not read.

citations.title: Delegation of Nursing Functions
citations.requirement: Chapter title confirmed from the link in .10A(9). The licensee must have a policy ensuring compliance with this chapter. Chapter text was not read.

citations.title: Criminal History Records Check for Individuals Who Work for an Adult Dependent Care Program
citations.requirement: Cited in .11B together with Health-General §19-1902 et seq. as the basis for criminal history checks. Chapter text was not read.

citations.title: Criminal history records check (as cited in COMAR 10.22.02.11B)
citations.requirement: COMAR 10.22.02.11B cites §19-1902 et seq. The fact-checked research cites '§19-1901 et seq.'. Confirm the exact starting section against the statute before finalizing. Statute text was not fetched.

citations.title: Fundamental rights (as cited in COMAR 10.22.02.10A(2))
citations.requirement: COMAR requires the licensee to have a policy ensuring fundamental rights in accordance with this section. Statute text was not fetched.

citations.title: Confidentiality (as cited in COMAR 10.22.02.10A(4) and .14E(7))
citations.requirement: COMAR requires the licensee to have a confidentiality policy in accordance with this section. The standing committee must also keep confidentiality under it. Statute text was not fetched.

citations.title: Reporting of suspected abuse, neglect, self-neglect or exploitation of a vulnerable adult
citations.requirement: Not in the fact-checked research and not fetched. Cited from general knowledge of Maryland's adult abuse reporting law. VERIFY before use. The DDA incident policy and local APS procedures control the details.

citations.cite: DDA Policy on Reportable Incidents and Investigations (PORII)
citations.title: DDA reportable incident procedures
citations.requirement: COMAR 10.22.02.10A(7) requires incidents to be reported and investigated 'in accordance with the Administration's procedures on reportable incidents'. The current PORII was not fetched, so incident levels, deadlines and forms must be copied from the current DDA PORII before finalizing.

citations.cite: Community Pathways Waiver, Appendix C — Community Living – Group Home
citations.title: Service definition, residence requirements, provider standards
citations.requirement: Taken from the fact-checked research (S8). Maximum 4 participants per residence unless previously approved by DDA, with private bedrooms. Services available 24/7 with back-up and emergency support. Staff are 18+ with First Aid/CPR and an in-person skills check. Medication Technician certification (Board of Nursing) for unlicensed staff who give medication. RN delegation. Transportation is included in the daily rate. Room and board are collected from the resident. Retainer days are up to 18 per person per year. No payment to relatives, legal guardians or legally responsible persons. Provider needs 5 years of DD residential experience.

citations.title: Financial accountability
citations.requirement: Taken from the fact-checked research (S9). Bill only services authorized in the approved PCP and Detailed Service Authorization in LTSSMaryland. Room and board are excluded from the rate. EVV is required for Personal Supports and Respite, not for CL–GH.

citations.title: HCBS settings requirements
citations.requirement: Taken from the fact-checked research (S52). Provider-owned or controlled residential settings need a lease or equivalent agreement, privacy, lockable doors, roommate choice, and access to food and visitors.

citations.title: Additional requirements for provider-owned or controlled residential settings
citations.requirement: Cited in the fact-checked research checklist for lockable bedroom doors and resident control of space. Any modification of these conditions must be supported by a specific assessed need and documented in the person-centered plan.

citations.title: Bloodborne pathogens (OSHA)
citations.requirement: Incorporated by reference in COMAR 10.22.02.11C(3). All staff and care providers must be trained in blood-borne pathogens in accordance with OSHA guidelines before independent duties.

citations.title: Earned sick and safe leave
citations.requirement: Taken from the fact-checked research (S40). Employees accrue 1 hour per 30 hours worked, up to 40 hours per year. Leave is paid when the employer has 15 or more employees.

citations.cite: Maryland Wage and Hour Law facts (MD Labor)
citations.title: State and local minimum wage
citations.requirement: Taken from the fact-checked research (S39). State minimum is $15.00/hr. Montgomery County is $18.00 (51+ employees), $16.50 (11–50 employees, and certain nonprofit and Medicaid-funded home care providers) and $15.95 (10 or fewer). Howard County is $16.00 and Prince George's County is $15.30 (as of July 1, 2026).

citations.cite: DDA Addendum for Participation in Maryland Medical Assistance Program — PT 90 DDA
citations.title: Separate MA number per licensed site
citations.requirement: Taken from the fact-checked research (S30). Each licensed site needs its own 'DDA Licensed Site MA' number. Medicaid enrollment, revalidation and SDAT good-standing checks run through MPRIME (PT 36-27); losing SDAT good standing causes immediate suspension.

citations.cite: Provider Portal Residential Services 2023 Billing Update (Jan 27, 2023)
citations.title: Number of People Authorized / retainer days
citations.requirement: Taken from the fact-checked research (S62). 'Number of People Authorized' (people living in the home and present, or on retainer days, max 18 per year) drives the residential billing rate. Example: when a resident leaves a 4-person home, the other three move from $403.30 to $355.23 per day.

citations.title: Staff Training Form — Developmental Disabilities Services
citations.requirement: Taken from the fact-checked research (S61). DDA form for documenting the COMAR 10.22.02.11C and D training topics.

citations.cite: DDA Addendum for Licensed Services and Sites (MDH Form DD.ADD.1.0, 06.02.2022)
citations.title: Site addendum with Community Settings Rule attestation
citations.requirement: Taken from the fact-checked research (S59). Lists each site, capacity requested and proposed occupancy date, and includes the Community Settings Rule attestation. Also asks whether the site is wheelchair accessible.

citations.cite: DDA New Site Visit Checklist (Community Settings Rule), Nov 14, 2022
citations.title: New site inspection form
citations.requirement: Taken from the fact-checked research (S60). Covers institutional or isolating characteristics, heightened scrutiny (including proximity to the provider's other sites) and settings-rule items.

policies.title: Health and Safety Needs Met per the Individual Plan; Implementation of Supports and Daily Documentation
state_specifics: Each person's health and safety needs as identified in the IP are met and documented (COMAR 10.22.02.10A(1))
Staffing levels and patterns are those determined in the IP (COMAR 10.22.08.04A)
Document IP implementation in the record kept at the site (.13B)
Services are available 24/7 with back-up and emergency support
Section numbers for IP timelines in COMAR 10.22.05 are unverified; pull them before finalizing

policies.title: Fundamental Rights, HCBS Settings Requirements, Rights Restrictions and Individual Choice
state_specifics: Ensure fundamental rights under Health-General §7-1002 (COMAR 10.22.02.10A(2)); read COMAR 10.22.04.03 text before finalizing
Provider-controlled homes need a lease or equivalent agreement, privacy, lockable bedroom doors, roommate choice, and access to food and visitors
Any modification of a settings-rule condition needs a specific assessed need documented in the person-centered plan (441.301(c)(4)(vi))
The standing committee reviews rights restrictions not related to challenging behavior and sets time frames (.14E)
Services are delivered in ways that promote choice (A(3)); sign the Community Settings Rule attestation on the site addendum

policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality and HIPAA
state_specifics: Confidentiality for each individual per Health-General §7-1010 (COMAR 10.22.02.10A(4))
Standing committee members must keep confidentiality under §7-1010 (.14E(7))
Electronic records must comply with HIPAA privacy and security rules and be backed up off-site (.13E)
Records are kept at the site where the person is served; release only with valid authorization or as the law requires

policies.title: Grievances and Complaints
state_specifics: Implement a grievance process with safeguards against retaliation for filing any grievance (COMAR 10.22.02.10A(5))
Give individuals and proponents enough information to use the process (.10D); see DG-01
Include OHCQ DD complaint line 410-402-8100 / 877-402-8220 in the notice
Log each grievance, the response and the outcome, and review trends in the QA system

policies.title: Nondiscrimination and Communication Access
state_specifics: Services are provided without discrimination (COMAR 10.22.02.10A(6))
Written policy to prevent employment discrimination and written job descriptions for every position (.11E)
Provide interpreters, accessible formats and communication supports to individuals and proponents
The site addendum asks whether the home is wheelchair accessible; track accommodations

policies.title: Reportable Incidents and Investigations
state_specifics: Report and investigate all incidents under DDA's Policy on Reportable Incidents and Investigations (PORII); the reviewer form cites the 10/1/2007 revision
Copy incident levels, deadlines and forms from the current DDA PORII; they were not verified here
The standing committee reviews the incident protocol and all incidents; members involved in an incident may not decide it (.14E)
OHCQ starts Priority 1 (immediate jeopardy) investigations within 2 working days (.03)
Respond to OHCQ findings with a plan of correction at the exit conference or within 10 working days (.04E)

policies.title: Medication Administration (MATP) and Compliance with Nursing Delegation (COMAR 10.27.11)
state_specifics: Administer medication per DDA's medication curriculum (MATP) (COMAR 10.22.02.10A(8); .12D)
Unit-dose packaging for oral solids unless the IP says otherwise; separate packaging for absent individuals
Request pharmacy-generated MARs, TARs and physician order forms
Unlicensed staff who give medication or treatments must be Board of Nursing Medication Technicians under RN delegation (10.27.11)
Follow the detailed procedures in NU-01 through NU-07

policies.title: Positive Behavior Support, Behavior Plans and Medications Used to Modify Behavior
state_specifics: Anyone whose behaviors require intervention gets the safeguards in COMAR 10.22.10 (COMAR 10.22.02.10A(10))
Behavior plan content and approval follow .10.05; medications to modify behavior follow .10.07; monitoring follows .10.11 (rule text not read; confirm before finalizing)
The standing committee approves every behavior plan that uses restrictive techniques (.14E(1)(d))
Track restrictive techniques in the QA system: who, which technique, date/time, emergency vs. plan, and effectiveness (.14B)
Use proactive, person-centered supports first and document that less restrictive options were tried

policies.title: Restrictive Interventions, Restraint and Seclusion
state_specifics: Restrictive techniques are used only as allowed by COMAR 10.22.10.06 and the specific restraint rules (.08 physical; .09 mechanical; .10 chemical); rule text not read
Standing committee approval is required before use in a behavior plan (.14E(1)(d))
Log every use and review it in QA (.14B)
Any use outside a plan is an emergency use: report it as an incident under the PORII
Staff may use only techniques they are trained in

policies.title: Payment for Property Damage
state_specifics: An individual may be required to pay for property damage only if the IP shows all five conditions in COMAR 10.22.02.10A(11)
(a) a documented history of destructive behavior in the behavior plan; (b) a BP that addresses it
(c) evidence the individual has the ability to pay
(d) the standing committee has reviewed and approved the payment
(e) the licensee has reported the approval to the Regional Director

policies.title: Informed Consent, Surrogate Decision-Making and Decision-Making Support
state_specifics: Comply with Health-General §5-605 (surrogate decision-making) (COMAR 10.22.02.10A(12))
Use supported decision-making and plain-language information before seeking any consent
Identify the legal decision-maker or proponent for each person and keep documentation in the record
Do not use staff or board members as surrogates (see PA-12)

policies.title: Conflict of Interest
state_specifics: No financial or personal conflict of interest for governing body members, staff, care providers, volunteers or standing committee members (COMAR 10.22.02.10A(13))
Board members and employees may not own property leased back to the licensee (.08C(9))
Employees and their immediate family may not be voting board members (.08)
Collect annual conflict of interest disclosures and record recusals

policies.title: Fiscal Practices (Generally Accepted Accounting Practices)
state_specifics: Fiscal affairs are conducted per generally accepted accounting practices (COMAR 10.22.02.10A(14))
The board approves the budget (.08C)
Keep room-and-board collections separate from Medicaid billing
Keep SDAT good standing and MA numbers current

policies.title: Personal Funds and Property Management
state_specifics: A(15)(a): a system to ensure funds are used for the individual's needs and preferences
A(15)(b): keep personal funds separate from licensee funds, and transfer them promptly when the person leaves
A(15)(c): the individual has timely access to funds
A(15)(d): provide an accounting of funds on request
A(15)(e): credit interest to the individual if the account bears interest; room and board is collected from the resident under a written agreement

policies.title: Infection Prevention, Standard Precautions and Safety Precautions
state_specifics: Implement State and federal safety precautions, infection control and standard precautions (COMAR 10.22.02.10A(16))
OSHA bloodborne pathogens training before independent duties (.11C(3))
Training on communicable diseases within 3 months of hire (.11D)
Provide PPE, an exposure control plan and post-exposure follow-up

policies.title: Individuals Not Performing Paid Staff Duties; Household Duties
state_specifics: Individuals do not perform duties of paid staff (COMAR 10.22.02.10A(18))
An individual does only household duties shared by the household, activities documented in the IP, or work paid as part of a training program (A(19))
Document any household-task agreement in the IP and respect choice
Staff-assigned chores such as cleaning common areas for the agency are not allowed

policies.category: B(1) through B(7) – Emergency plan for ALUs/GHs
policies.title: Emergency Plan: Evacuation, Transportation, 72-Hour Shelter-in-Place, Identification and Role of Family
state_specifics: Written plan for all types of emergencies with before, during and after procedures (COMAR 10.22.02.10B(1))
Cover evacuation, transportation or 72-hour shelter-in-place for individuals and staff (B(1)(a))
Everyone has ID with current health and contact information that is immediately accessible during evacuation (B(1)(d))
Define the role of the resident, family or legal representative during evacuation (B(1)(e))
Keep a written fire evacuation plan in each home (.12B)

policies.category: B(1) through B(7) – Emergency plan for ALUs/GHs
policies.title: Emergency and Fire Drills and After-Action Reports
state_specifics: Hold an annual practice drill coordinated with local emergency planners for sheltering in place or evacuating (B(1)(b))
Prepare an after-action report and improvement plan after drills, evaluating the plan and taking corrective action (B(1)(c))
Run enough drills to meet A(17) (adequate drills); the rule sets no fixed number, so set a schedule that covers all shifts
Smoke detectors and fire extinguishers are working and updated (.12B)

policies.category: B(1) through B(7) – Emergency plan for ALUs/GHs
policies.title: Alternate Sites, Redundant Communication and Notifications
state_specifics: Arrange medical needs and accommodations for individuals and staff at alternate facilities or shelters (B(1)(f))
Communication protocol with redundant means among all parties (B(1)(g))
Notify families, staff and DDA (B(2)); DDA regional offices: CMRO 410-234-8200, ESRO 410-572-5920, SMRO 301-362-5100, WMRO 301-791-4670
Notification of any incident follows the PORII

policies.category: B(1) through B(7) – Emergency plan for ALUs/GHs
policies.title: Emergency Staff Coverage, Recall and Continuity of Operations
state_specifics: Plan staff coverage for ongoing shelter in place or evacuation (B(3)(a))
Identify staff available to report or remain during extended periods (B(3)(b))
Staff notification and recall contingency procedures (B(3)(c))
Continuity of operations plan (B(4)) that keeps 24/7 coverage with back-up

policies.category: B(1) through B(7) – Emergency plan for ALUs/GHs
policies.title: Back-up of Records, Sharing the Plan with Emergency Management, and Family Summary
state_specifics: Back up and store off-site electronic records of individuals, staff and the facility for emergency access (B(5)(a))
Provide an electronic copy of the plan when local, State or federal emergency management requests it (B(5)(b))
Share the plan with local emergency management organizations (B(6))
Give families an executive summary on request (B(7))
Electronic records must also meet HIPAA security rules and be backed up off-site (.13E)

policies.category: C – Staff awareness and implementation of policies
policies.title: Staff Awareness and Implementation of Policies; Policy Review and Document Control
state_specifics: All staff, care providers, consultants and volunteers must know and carry out each adopted policy (COMAR 10.22.02.10C)
Document orientation and a signed acknowledgment at hire and after each revision
Review the policy manual at least annually and whenever the rules change; keep a version log
Document training on the Staff Training Form

policies.category: D – Grievance process information for individuals and proponents
policies.title: Grievance Process Information for Individuals and Proponents
state_specifics: Give individuals and proponents enough information to use the grievance process effectively (COMAR 10.22.02.10D)
Provide it at admission and annually in plain language, accessible formats and the person's own language
Post OHCQ complaint contacts: 410-402-8100 / 877-402-8220
Explain anti-retaliation protections and who will help file a grievance

policies.category: Nursing – Medication P&P, Reporting/Communication and the RN Role
policies.title: Medication: Obtaining Orders and Medications
state_specifics: Medications are given only on a current written prescriber order
Request pharmacy-generated MARs, TARs and physician order forms (.12D)
Unit-dose packaging for oral solids unless the IP says otherwise
Follow the current MTTP and DDA medication curriculum for transcription and order verification

policies.category: Nursing – Medication P&P, Reporting/Communication and the RN Role
policies.title: Medication Administration and Storage
state_specifics: Only certified Medication Technicians (or licensed nurses) give medication
Store medication locked, separate by individual, and package medication for absent individuals separately (.12D)
Document each dose on the MAR at the time given

policies.category: Nursing – Medication P&P, Reporting/Communication and the RN Role
policies.title: Controlled Drugs
state_specifics: The reviewer cites MTTP 1:4-9; 2:1-9; 2:2-5; 2:2-7
Double-lock controlled drugs and count at every shift change with two signatures
Investigate and report discrepancies immediately; treat them as incidents under the PORII
Document destruction and disposal

policies.category: Nursing – Medication P&P, Reporting/Communication and the RN Role
policies.title: Medication Errors
state_specifics: The reviewer cites COMAR 10.27.11 and MTTP 2:3-17; 2:4-10
Notify the delegating RN and prescriber immediately and follow instructions
Report and review errors under the PORII and the QA system
Retrain or restrict the Medication Technician after an error as the RN directs

policies.category: Nursing – Medication P&P, Reporting/Communication and the RN Role
policies.title: Determining Ability to Self-Medicate
state_specifics: The reviewer cites MTTP Chapter 8
The RN assesses ability and supports needed; record the result in the IP
Reassess at least annually and after any change of condition
Support the person's choice to self-administer when assessed as safe; store medication so the person can reach it

policies.category: Nursing – Medication P&P, Reporting/Communication and the RN Role
policies.title: Reporting and Communication of Health Information
state_specifics: Staff report changes in condition to the delegating RN and document them
Make medical information readily accessible to emergency personnel (.13C)
Hand-off between shifts is documented, and health communication is shared with prescribers, family and the case coordinator as authorized

policies.category: Nursing – Medication P&P, Reporting/Communication and the RN Role
policies.title: The RN Role, Nursing Delegation and Health Care Coordination
state_specifics: The reviewer cites COMAR 10.27.11 and MTTP 6-5
The delegating RN delegates and supervises CMT tasks and audits MARs
The RN coordinates HRST and health care follow-up for each resident
Nursing Support Services: ask DDA whether hours are authorized separately per resident (W5804)
Confirm RN licensure annually

policies.category: Explanation of all items checked 'No', with a compliance plan
policies.title: Compliance Plan for Required Items Not Met
state_specifics: Explain every item checked 'No' on the DDA policy review form and attach a compliance plan with owner and due date
Track the plan to completion and report status to the governing body
Submit revised policies to OHCQ and DDA as requested
Submit policies to OHCQ within 30 days of DDA approval

policies.title: Organization, Governing Body and Program Director Responsibilities
state_specifics: Licensee must be a Maryland corporation or registered foreign corporation (COMAR 10.22.02.02A(1))
Board must include at least one person with a DD, one family member and one person with DD experience; 75% must live in MD or within 100 miles (.08)
Employees and their immediate family cannot be voting members
Bylaws cover oversight, compliance, mission/budget/policy approval, conflict of interest, POC responses and PSP approval (.08C)
Governing body reviews the Program Service Plan at least every 3 years (.09C)

policies.title: Licensure, Site Approval, Licensed Capacity and Provider Agreements
state_specifics: A license is required to provide community residential services (COMAR 10.22.02.01-1)
DDA approval at least 30 days in advance to open, close or relocate a site (.05)
Do not exceed licensed capacity without Director approval (60 days plus one 60-day extension) (.06)
File renewal at least 60 days before the license expires (.02B)
Each licensed site needs its own MA number (PT 90 DDA); keep SDAT good standing in MPRIME

policies.title: Quality Assurance, Standing Committee, Data Review and Mortality Review
state_specifics: Submit the QA plan and substantive changes to DDA for approval (COMAR 10.22.02.14A)
QA is focused on individual choice and satisfaction, with measurable outcomes and trend analysis (.14B)
Standing committee has equal numbers of staff and non-employees and reviews incidents, restrictive behavior plans and rights restrictions (.14E)
Review each death in the mortality review process and report results to the committee
Make changes based on QA data and keep records (.14C)

policies.title: Medicaid Compliance, Billing and Service Documentation
state_specifics: Bill only services in the approved PCP and Detailed Service Authorization in LTSSMaryland (W5600, per person per day)
Enter the correct 'Number of People Authorized' on each claim; the rate follows the number of people living in the home
Retainer days up to 18 per person per year; the person still counts toward home size
EVV is not required for CL–GH; it is required for Personal Supports and Respite
Screen staff and owners against the OIG exclusion list; payment may lag up to 180 days

policies.title: Referral, Admission, Residency Agreement, Room and Board, and Transition In
state_specifics: Maximum 4 residents per home unless DDA previously approved; private bedrooms (sharing only by choice)
Do not exceed licensed capacity (.06)
Each resident has a lease or equivalent residency agreement under the settings rule
Room and board is excluded from the Medicaid rate and collected from the resident under a written agreement; set an affordable amount
Roommate choice and a trial-experience option should be documented

policies.title: Person-Centered Planning and the Individual Plan
state_specifics: The IP as defined in COMAR 10.22.05 must be in the record (.13B)
Services are authorized in the PCP in LTSSMaryland
Settings-rule modifications must be justified and documented in the plan
Shared dedicated hours must be documented in each PCP
Pull IP timelines from COMAR 10.22.05 before finalizing; the sections were not verified

policies.title: Community Integration and Employment Choice
state_specifics: The home must be integrated in the community and not gated or isolated; DDA's site checklist tests proximity to the provider's other sites
Residents have access to the community, visitors and food at any time
Offer information about employment and day service options and document the person's choice
Staff training in community integration within 3 months of hire (.11D)

policies.title: Transition, Discharge and Termination of Services
state_specifics: Terminate services only for good cause with the Director's written approval (COMAR 10.22.02.02G)
Give the Director 90 days' written notice
Give the individual and proponent written notice of the right to a hearing under COMAR 10.22.16, and copy the regional office and team
Services are considered terminated after 60 consecutive days' absence unless the Director decides otherwise
Transfer personal funds, records and property promptly when the person leaves

policies.title: Health Monitoring, Seizures and Choking Risk
state_specifics: Pre-service training on seizure disorders is required before independent duties (.11C)
Staff hold First Aid/CPR with an in-person skills check (American Red Cross or equivalent)
Each person's health and safety risks (seizure, choking) are in the IP with staff protocols
The RN reviews risk, including HRST results, and updates plans after changes
Nursing Support Services may be needed after a health change or hospital discharge

policies.title: Change of Condition and Emergency Medical Care
state_specifics: Call 911 for emergencies and then notify the RN, guardian/proponent and DDA as the PORII requires
Make medical information readily accessible to emergency personnel (.13C)
Retainer days up to 18 per year cover hospitalization
Document the event and follow up on any change of condition in the record

policies.title: Death of an Individual
state_specifics: Report a death immediately under the current DDA PORII and notify family or proponent
Keep the person's records at least 6 years after death (.13D)
Preserve the scene and medication records as directed by authorities
Include the death in the mortality review (see GOV-03)
Transfer personal funds and property per PA-14

policies.title: Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation Prevention and Reporting
state_specifics: Report and investigate all incidents under the PORII (COMAR 10.22.02.10A(7))
Report suspected abuse to the authorities as Maryland law requires; confirm statute before finalizing
No retaliation against reporters
Criminal history checks before hire (.11B; Health-General §19-1902 et seq.; COMAR 12.15.03)
OHCQ complaint line 410-402-8100 / 877-402-8220

policies.title: Missing Person and Elopement
state_specifics: Immediate search protocol, then notify police, the guardian/proponent and DDA
Report as an incident under the PORII; take the timelines from the current PORII
Document each person's elopement risk and supports in the IP
Do not use locks or alarms on exits unless approved as a rights restriction

policies.title: Residential Environment, Accessibility, Fire Safety and Water Temperature
state_specifics: Meet local zoning (except as in Health-General §7-603), State and local building codes and life-safety requirements (.12A)
Home free of hazards and in good repair; adequate smoke detectors; working, updated fire extinguishers; written fire evacuation plan (.12B)
Water temperature at a maximum of 110°F unless every resident can regulate it safely and each IP documents this (.12C)
Lockable bedroom doors and resident control of their space (441.301(c)(4)(vi))
Document wheelchair accessibility on the site addendum

policies.title: Food, Nutrition and Modified Diets
state_specifics: Residents have access to food at any time under the settings rule
Modified diets and texture needs are in the IP and ordered by a prescriber or dietitian
Staff are trained on diets and choking protocols
Honor food preferences and document choices

policies.title: Transportation and Vehicle Safety
state_specifics: Transportation is included in the daily rate; use the most cost-effective mode
Insure all vehicles; drivers need a valid driver's license
Staff are 18+ with First Aid/CPR
Include vehicle evacuation in emergency planning (see EP-01)

policies.title: Staffing Plan, Supervision and Awake Overnight Staff
state_specifics: Maryland sets no fixed staff ratio; analyze each person's needs and develop and implement a staffing plan (COMAR 10.22.02.11A)
Staffing levels and patterns follow the IP (10.22.08.04A)
Services available 24/7 at each licensed site with back-up and emergency support
DDA's rate for a 4-person home with overnight supervision funds 43.14 staff-hours per day
No relatives, legal guardians or legally responsible persons may be paid for this service

policies.title: Background Checks and Employee Registries
state_specifics: No employing or contracting with anyone whose criminal history indicates behavior potentially harmful to individuals (.11B)
Check everyone with direct contact before work: employees, contractors and volunteers
Cite COMAR 12.15.03 and Health-General §19-1902 et seq.; confirm the exact statute start section
Screen against the OIG exclusion list and the Maryland sanctioned provider list
Keep results on the Staff Criminal History form

policies.title: Direct Support Professional Orientation and Training
state_specifics: Before independent duties: job training, DDA-approved training on seizures, behavior change, managing disruptive behavior, medication administration and aging, and OSHA bloodborne pathogens (.11C)
Within 3 months of hire: community integration, individual-directed planning, characteristics of people served, First Aid/CPR, rights, communicable diseases, choice, and communication skills (.11D)
Document training on the Staff Training Form DD.APP.1.1
Medication Technician certification for unlicensed staff who give medication
DDA's rate assumes about 27.3 training hours per FTE per year

policies.title: Personnel Records, Employee Health Screening and Wage and Leave Compliance
state_specifics: Written job descriptions for every position and an anti-discrimination policy (.11E)
Keep training, background-check and CMT records in each personnel file
TB and health screening: no COMAR requirement was verified; set per licensee policy and confirm with the local health department
State minimum wage is $15.00; check county minimums (Montgomery, Howard, Prince George's)
Earned sick and safe leave: 1 hour per 30 worked, up to 40 hours per year, paid at 15 or more employees

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
state_specifics: No conflict of interest for staff, care providers and volunteers (A(13))
Individuals do not perform paid staff duties (A(18))
Staff may not borrow from, sell to or take money or gifts from individuals
Relatives, legal guardians and legally responsible persons may not be paid for this service
Misconduct is reported as an incident under the PORII

policies.title: Individual Records and Retention
state_specifics: Keep each individual's records at the site where the person is served (.13A)
Minimum contents: identifying information, emergency contact, next of kin, physician, diagnosis, allergies, medication list, the IP and IP implementation documentation (.13B)
Keep records at least 6 years, even if the person leaves or dies (.13D)
Electronic records must meet HIPAA, be backed up and be stored off-site (.13E)

policies.title: Required Reports to the State, Inspections and Plans of Correction
state_specifics: OHCQ inspects announced and unannounced at least annually, plus complaint visits (.04C–D)
Plan of correction at the exit conference or within 10 working days; the OHCQ Director may extend up to 30 days (.04E)
Resubmit an unacceptable POC within 10 working days (.04F)
Report incidents under the PORII
Seek DDA approval 30 days ahead for new sites, closures or relocations (.05), and report capacity overages (.06)

official.notes: The reviewer works from the two-page DH Form DD.APP.1.1 (02/18) checklist. The provider submits it together with a written policies and procedures document. For each item, the provider marks Present Yes, No or N/A, and marks whether the policy was modified since the last OHCQ survey. Every item marked 'No' needs an explanation and a compliance plan in the box at the end of the form. The safest way to organize the manual is to follow the form's numbering (A(1)–A(19), B(1)–B(7), C, D, then Nursing). Put the item ID on the policy that satisfies it, so the reviewer can match each box to a page. The form has no numbers for the seven Nursing items. I labeled them Nursing-1 to Nursing-7 in the order the form lists them. These seven items cite specific Medication Training and Technical Procedures (MTTP) sections, so the medication policies should reference those sections. The DDA Qualified Provider Application (Provider Application 9.19.25) says that if DDA approves the application, the policies and procedures must be submitted to OHCQ within 30 days of approval. The A(8) and A(9) wording on the form is shorter than the regulation's. A(8) says 'MATP' on the form. The regulation refers to the Administration's curriculum on medication training. COMAR 10.22.02.10 sets no separate policy about staff training. Staff training is a separate DDA checklist, 'Staff Training – DDS (COMAR 10.22.02.11C&D)', which is also marked DH Form DD.APP.1.1 (02/18). It is a training-record form, not a policy list, so I left it out of the items. The regulation text I used for sub-items is the current version on regs.maryland.gov.
